title: AFC/M23 Captures Humura Commercial Center in Masisi, Presses Toward Walikale
detail: AFC/M23 took control of the Humura commercial center in the Nyamaboko 1er grouping of Masisi territory, North Kivu, on Sept 6-7 after violent clashes with Wazalendo fighters. Local sources said no human or material toll from the fighting had been communicated as of Sept 7. The capture extends AFC/M23 pressure toward neighboring Walikale territory, notably the Waloa Uroba and Waloa Yungu groupings, bringing the rebels closer to Langira and Ntoto — areas already absorbing displaced families fleeing the wider Masisi-Walikale fighting that began in late August.

confidenceReason: The territorial capture is corroborated by two independent Congolese outlets reporting on Sept 7; no casualty or material toll has been confirmed by either side.

title: AFC/M23 Attacks Kibundi and Mwima, Driving Eight Villages to Flee Toward Ntoto
detail: The security and humanitarian situation stayed tense through Monday, Sept 7 in Masisi and Walikale territories, North Kivu, after intense fighting over the weekend. AFC/M23 attacked FARDC- and Wazalendo-held positions at Kibundi and Mwima villages, in the Katoyi sector of Masisi's Nyamaboko I grouping, with bombardments also reported near Mindjendje that pushed government forces to withdraw toward Mpeti. Residents of at least eight villages fled to Ntoto, in Walikale's Waloa Uroba grouping, joining earlier arrivals from the Masisi-Walikale fighting; local notables said host communities remain overwhelmed and no official casualty or displacement count has been established.

confidenceReason: Reported by local notables and unnamed local sources via Radio Okapi and corroborated in CongoQuotidien's daily roundup; no FARDC, M23 or humanitarian-agency confirmation of casualty or displacement figures yet.
